extracted.intended_audience: NeurIPS 2024 reviewers (and area chairs assigning reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for reviewers evaluating NeurIPS 2024 submissions, covering required preparation, review form components (summary, strengths/weaknesses, ratings, etc.), expected review quality, reviewer conduct, and critical policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must acknowledge the Code of Conduct, maintain updated OpenReview profiles, and understand conflict-of-interest policies before beginning assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete these preparatory steps prior to starting review assignments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Quality Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: "The community depends on your high quality reviews to uphold the scientific quality of NeurIPS." Reviewers should provide substantiated, informative assessments rather than superficial evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide evidence-backed critiques and informative commentary; avoid cursory statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: Objective paper description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Succinctly and accurately summarize the paper's contributions, methods, and claims without editorializing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strengths/Weaknesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of a paper's strengths and weaknesses, explicitly considering originality, quality, clarity, and significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss both positive aspects and shortcomings with specifics tied to originality, methodological quality, clarity of presentation, and significance/impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Questions for Authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Points or clarifications where author responses could alter the reviewer's assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pose concrete, answerable questions that would materially affect evaluation; prioritize questions likely to change scores or acceptance decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the adequacy of the authors' discussion of the work's constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether authors have acknowledged limitations, failure modes, or generalizability concerns and whether those discussions are sufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Flagging cases that merit an ethics review when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and describe potential ethical issues (e.g., harms, misuse, dataset/privacy concerns) clearly so organizers can decide on an ethics review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerical Ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide numeric ratings on dimensions including soundness, presentation, and contribution using 1-4 scales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these structured ratings to reflect judgments on technical correctness (soundness), clarity/presentation, and the significance of the contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Assign an overall score on a 1-10 scale with detailed descriptors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the provided scale descriptors to map your holistic judgment (acceptability/impact) to a numeric overall score and justify with review text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidence Level
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate your certainty in the assessment using a 1-5 scale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report how confident you are in your evaluation based on familiarity with the topic, paper clarity, and any unresolved questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be Thoughtful with Early-Career Researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation that reviewers be considerate when evaluating submissions from early-career researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply judgment that recognizes potential inexperience; provide constructive guidance rather than harsh dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness and Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should remain fair and impartial in their assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid biases, base critiques on evidence in the paper, and evaluate work on its merits rather than author identity or institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide Constructive Feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should give actionable, constructive feedback to help authors improve their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggest concrete fixes, clarifications, or experiments when pointing out problems; aim to be helpful and specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Vague Statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are instructed to avoid vague, unsubstantiated claims in reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer precise, evidence-based comments over generic criticisms like "this is unclear" without elaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness / Respond Promptly to Deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should respond promptly to deadlines throughout the review timeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to bidding, review, discussion, and decision-phase dates specified in the Key Timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-Blind Reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Double-blind reviewing is maintained at the reviewer/area-chair level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not attempt to identify authors; follow anonymization expectations and avoid actions that would break double-blind procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Sub-Reviewers Permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: No sub-reviewers are permitted for reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not delegate review work to external/unauthorized collaborators or students; the assigned reviewer is responsible for the review content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code Execution Policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Code must run in isolated environments only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If evaluating provided code, execute it only in isolated/sandboxed environments per the policy to avoid security/privacy risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete confidentiality required for assigned submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share or discuss submission content outside the authorized review channels; respect the confidentiality of submitted materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Dual Submissions Allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions that are under consideration elsewhere (dual submissions) are not permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag suspected dual submissions or treat them according to conference policy; consider dual-submission status when assessing novelty/priority.
